products.superPrompt:
You are an experienced American-style mahjong instructor and a print designer. Write the complete content for a sellable, Canva-editable "Beginner Mahjong Class Kit" a new teacher can brand and use next week.

BUYER AND JOB: New independent mahjong instructors and club hosts running paid beginner classes. Classes fill faster than they can prepare; this kit gives them a ready 3-session course, handouts, admin sheets and promo templates under their own brand.

DELIVERABLE (US Letter 8.5x11 in portrait unless noted; I will also make an A4 copy, so keep 0.5 in margins and nothing essential in the outer 0.25 in):
1. Cover: "Beginner Mahjong Class Kit" with an editable [YOUR CLASS NAME] line.
2. Instructor guide (1 page): how to use the kit, materials for 4 tables of 4, a 90-minute session format.
3. Session plans 1-3 (1 page each): goals, minute-by-minute agenda, demo script, 5 common mistakes, take-home practice.
4. Student handouts:
- Session 1 "Meet the Tiles": a 2-page tile ID chart for a 152-tile American set (Dots, Bams, Craks 1-9, Winds, Dragons, Flowers, Jokers) with counts and the exact characters for every tile that carries them; building the walls and the deal; a 20-term glossary.
- Session 2 "The Charleston": a step-by-step walk-through with a described pass diagram, when blind passes are allowed, the optional courtesy pass, and "jokers are never passed".
- Session 3 "Jokers, Calling and Your First Game": joker rules, joker exchange, calling a discard, dead hands, basic payment, and 4 original practice patterns.
- Turn-order quick card (half page, 2 per sheet).
5. Admin: class sign-in sheet (16 rows: name, email or phone, Session 1-3 checkboxes, paid); student progress checklist (12 skills x 16 students grid); "First Game" certificate (landscape; editable student, date, instructor).
6. Marketing: class flyer (editable date, venue, price, booking link, QR placeholder); 3 Instagram posts at 1080x1350 px and 2 Stories at 1080x1920 px (announcement, what you'll learn, last spots), each with a caption.
7. Heritage page "Where Mahjong Comes From": origins in 19th-century China, the 1920s spread to the US, an American league formed in 1937 that still issues a yearly card, and a table comparing Chinese/Hong Kong, Japanese Riichi and American play (tile count, jokers, Charleston, winning hand). Warm, factual, respectful.

DESIGN: Fonts DM Serif Display (headings), Inter (body), Noto Serif SC (Chinese characters). Palette "Jade Table": Tile Ivory #F7F1E3 background, Jade #2F7D6D primary, Ink #1F2A36 text, Cinnabar #B8432F accents, Bamboo Gold #D9A441 highlights, Mist #DCE8E3 panels. Give layout notes for every page (blocks, columns, icon spots, font sizes).

CONTENT RULES:
- Original wording; plain English, about 8th-grade reading level; friendly instructor voice.
- Accuracy: an American set has 152 tiles (108 suit tiles, 16 winds, 12 dragons, 8 flowers, 8 jokers); each wall is 19 stacks two high; East starts with 14 tiles, the others 13; the first Charleston passes right, across, left, the optional second passes left, across, right. Craks show 一 to 九 above 萬; winds 東 南 西 北; Red Dragon 中, Green Dragon 發, White Dragon a blank or framed tile. Chinese/Hong Kong (144 tiles) and Riichi (136 tiles) hands are built from four sets and a pair; American hands must match the current card. Re-check every count and character. Where rules vary, write "house rules vary" instead of guessing.
- Practice patterns: invent simple teaching combinations, label each "Practice pattern for learning only, not from any official card", use no year numbers, and do not copy, mimic or name any official card's sections or hands.
- Mention the card only as: "Each student needs their own copy of the current official card (sold separately)."

DIFFERENTIATION: Existing printables are player cheat sheets. This kit serves the teacher: lesson flow, scripts, admin and promotion in one brand system, plus honest heritage framing.

CONSTRAINTS: No league names or logos, no tile-brand or designer-set names or artwork, no celebrities, no song lyrics, no faux-"Asian" novelty fonts or stereotyped imagery, no claims about health, income or results.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Page by page as "PAGE n | Title | Size | Layout | Exact text", tables written as tables, ready to paste into Canva. Finish with a 1-page free sample (the Charleston walk-through, footer "Sample from [YOUR SHOP NAME]"). If you run out of space, stop at the end of a page and wait for me to type "continue".

SELF-CHECK before answering: (1) every page is present; (2) tile counts total 152 and every character is correct; (3) both Charleston orders are right; (4) no official card hands, names or logos; (5) the heritage page credits Chinese origins without stereotypes. Fix anything that fails, then answer.

assembly: Day 1 (about 3 h): paste the super prompt into Claude or ChatGPT, type 'continue' until all pages arrive, and copy everything into one Google Doc. Proofread the rules pages against the current official rulebook, or ask an experienced American-style player to read them; fix anything marked 'house rules vary'.

In Canva create a US Letter (8.5 x 11 in) design; save the six 'Jade Table' hex codes and the fonts DM Serif Display, Inter and Noto Serif SC (search Canva's font list; if a font is missing, use the closest serif or a Chinese-capable sans). Turn on rulers and add 0.5 in margin guides, then build three master layouts: handout, admin grid and marketing.

Build the tile ID chart from Canva shapes, not AI images: rounded rectangles about 0.9 x 1.2 in with Tile Ivory fill and a 2 pt Ink border; type the Arabic numerals and the Chinese characters from the AI output (一 to 九, 萬, 東 南 西 北, 中, 發) in the Chinese font; draw Dots as circles and Bams as rounded sticks; label every tile in English. Check each tile against your own set.

Paste the text page by page, add the pattern and icons, and make the sign-in sheet and progress checklist with Canva's Table element (10-11 pt body text). Put editable fields in [brackets] and keep the free-sample footer only on the sample page.

Make the A4 version: duplicate the design at custom size 210 x 297 mm (or use Resize with Canva Pro or its free trial) and fix any text that reflows. Create the social templates as separate designs at 1080 x 1350 px (3 posts) and 1080 x 1920 px (2 Stories).
Export Share > Download > PDF Print (Canva's 300 DPI print setting), no crop marks, for the Letter and A4 versions; export the 1-page Charleston sample as its own PDF.

For each editable design use Share > Template link, test every link in a private browser window, then make a 2-page US Letter 'Access your templates' PDF with the links as buttons and 5 numbered steps (open, Use template, edit, print, save).

Make 7 listing images at 2700 x 2025 px (4:3): hero mockup, what's-inside grid, tile chart close-up, Charleston page, admin pages, heritage page and social templates; record a 10-15 second flip-through video for Etsy (it plays without sound).

Publish on Etsy as a digital listing with three files (Letter PDF, A4 PDF, templates PDF; Etsy allows up to 5 files of 20 MB each). On Gumroad, upload the same files at the same price and the sample as a separate $0+ product so downloaders join your email list.
products.listingPrompt:
You are an Etsy SEO copywriter. Write the Etsy listing for my digital download "Beginner Mahjong Class Kit" for new mahjong instructors and club hosts who teach beginner classes.
Product facts: 3-session American-style beginner course; instructor guide and 3 session plans; student handouts (tile ID chart, Charleston walk-through, jokers and calling, turn-order card, glossary); class sign-in sheet; student progress checklist; "First Game" certificate; class flyer; 3 Instagram post and 2 Story templates; heritage page on mahjong's Chinese origins and its variants. Formats: US Letter and A4 PDFs plus editable template links that open in a free Canva account. Instant download. [ADD YOUR PAGE COUNT]

Produce:
1. TITLE under 140 characters that starts with the buyer's search phrase (choose from "Mahjong Lesson Plan", "Mahjong Teacher Kit", "Mahjong Class Handouts"), then the key contents (handouts, sign-in sheet, certificate, flyer, editable template). Sentence case, no ALL CAPS, at most 3 keyword phrases. Show the character count.
2. 13 TAGS, each 20 characters or fewer (show the count after each), no tag repeated, drawn from phrases like: mahjong lesson plan, mahjong teacher kit, mahjong class kit, mahjong handout, learn mahjong, mahjong beginner, charleston guide, mahjong certificate, mahjong class flyer, mahjong sign in, teach mahjong, game night teacher, editable class kit.
3. DESCRIPTION: a 2-line opening for teachers (no hype); "What's included" as a page-by-page bullet list; file formats and sizes; how delivery works (download from Etsy Purchases, open the "Access your templates" PDF, click each link, choose "Use template" to copy it into your own free account, edit, print or download); what is not included (tiles; the official card: "students need their own current official card, sold separately; this shop is not affiliated with any league or tile brand"); license (use for your own classes and students; do not resell or share the files or links); a line that illustrations were made with AI assistance and designed by me; and a 5-question FAQ (Can I add my logo? Is this American style? Can a copy shop print it? Do I need a paid design account? Can I teach other styles with it?).
RULES: No trademarked or brand terms in the title or tags: no league names or abbreviations, no tile-brand or designer-set names, no software brand names. One plain compatibility note about the editing app may appear in the description only. No claims that the kit will fill classes, earn money or guarantee results. Do not describe mahjong as exotic or mysterious. Output in this order: Title, Tags, Description.

pricing.rationale: Above the $1-12 player cheat sheets because this is a teaching tool with editable admin and promo pages for paid classes; $19 matches the input's validation test. Drop to $14 or split the kit if favorites do not convert; move toward $29 only after reviews and a sessions 4-6 add-on.

marketing.positioning: The teacher's side of the mahjong boom: a done-for-you, editable beginner course (3 lessons, handouts, admin sheets, promo templates) that a new instructor brands as their own, with a heritage page that credits mahjong's Chinese origins. Not another player cheat sheet.

launchPlan.action: Publish the $19 Etsy listing and the Gumroad product, plus the free Charleston sample on Gumroad. If you are also building the Analog Bag Refill Pack, build that first (its deadline is seasonal) and this kit on Oct 8-12.

Start Etsy Ads at $1/day. Publish 5 Pinterest pins (tile chart, Charleston page, sign-in sheet, certificate, flyer) at 1000 x 1500 px linking to the Etsy listing. Put the Gumroad sample link in your Instagram bio.

Build a list of 30 Instagram accounts that teach mahjong or run clubs (search 'mahjong lessons', 'mahjong classes', 'mahjong club' plus city names). Send the first 6 personal DMs offering the free sample, with no hard sell.
Post Reel 1: a 20-second flip-through of the kit. Pin 2 more designs.
Check Etsy Stats (views, favorites, ad clicks, search terms). If views are under about 15/day, raise ads to $2/day. Continue DMs (3 per weekday).

Post Reel 2: 'the Charleston in 60 seconds' using the handout. Where self-promotion is allowed (check the community rules), post the free sample once in 1-2 Facebook groups for mahjong teachers or organizers. Add a 'pairs with' line linking the Club Organizer Kit if it is live.
Ads end. Send the last DMs (30 total). Email the sample downloaders once with a 72-hour 15% code. Compare ad clicks to sales before deciding whether to keep ads on.
Refresh the listing: make the best-saved pin design the first photo and swap 3 tags for search terms that actually appeared in Etsy Stats.

Go/pivot/stop check. Continue if at least 3 sales, or at least 2% conversion on at least 300 listing views. Pivot if views and favorites come but no sales: split into a $7 Student Handout Pack and a $12 Admin & Promo Pack. Stop if under 100 views after 3 weeks with ads, or if you find instructor kits are abundant at lower prices.

asymmetry.downside: About 16 hours of build time, up to $28 in Etsy Ads and $0.20 in listing fees. No inventory and no deadline.
asymmetry.upside: Zero marginal cost per sale; sells on Etsy, Gumroad and Payhip at once; evergreen while classes keep forming (instructor tools likely stay relevant through 2027); every buyer is a teacher who can buy the add-on, club and holiday kits, and an instructor email list compounds. The 21-day test gives a clear answer by Nov 3.
asymmetry.badBetIf: Etsy already has many instructor kits at or under $10 (check page 1-2 for 'mahjong lesson plan' and 'mahjong teacher' before building), you cannot get the rules pages checked by an experienced player, or you are not willing to message instructors directly, because Etsy discovery alone may be too slow for a narrow B2B niche.

risks: IP: reproducing any official card hand, the league's name or logo, or a designer tile set's artwork could get the listing removed; keep practice patterns clearly invented and the card mentioned only as 'sold separately'.

Cultural framing: a non-Asian seller 'refreshing' mahjong has drawn backlash before; keep the heritage page, avoid novelty 'Asian' fonts and stereotyped imagery, and make sure the Chinese characters are correct.
Rules errors would cost credibility with teachers; get the rules pages proofread before launch.
AI image models garble Chinese characters, so tile faces must be typed in Canva, not generated.
Narrow niche: the input could not verify how many instructor kits already exist; Etsy views may stay low without the DM outreach.
Platform rules: disclose AI-assisted artwork as Etsy's creativity standards require, and share Canva designs only as template links per Canva's content license (check both policies).

products.superPrompt:
You are a Google Sheets and Apps Script expert who also runs a weekly mahjong club. Build a sellable "Mahjong Club Organizer Kit": one Google Sheets workbook plus printable copy that a host copies and uses tonight.

BUYER AND JOB: People starting or running mahjong clubs, leagues and weekly open play, often with 30-55 players. Single-game score cards already exist; these hosts need multi-table logistics: who sits where each round, who is confirmed or waitlisted, season standings and club money.

PART 1. Write one Google Apps Script function buildClubKit() (SpreadsheetApp only; no external calls, triggers or libraries) that I run once in a new blank spreadsheet (locale United States). It creates these tabs in order with headers, formulas, dropdowns, checkboxes, number formats, frozen header rows, column widths, colors and 12 rows of fictional sample data (invented first names only):
1. Start Here: what each tab does, a 6-step quick start, the rotation facts below in plain words, and "Use File > Make a copy to start".
2. Settings: B2 Club name; B3 Players tonight =COUNTIF(Tonight!B2:B33,"?*"); B4 Tables =MAX(1,ROUNDUP(B3/4,0)); B5 Rounds tonight (dropdown 1-8); B6 Season name; B7 Kitty opening balance; B8 =IF(B3>32,"Max 32 players per rotation","").
3. Roster: #, Name, Contact, Joined, Status (Active/Waitlist/Inactive), Dues paid (checkbox), Notes; 60 rows.
4. Sign-Up: B1 Event date; B2 Seats available (default 32); from row 5 columns Name, Signed up at, Cancelled (checkbox), Status =IF(A5="","",IF(C5=TRUE,"Cancelled",LET(n,SUMPRODUCT((A$5:A5<>"")*(C$5:C5<>TRUE)),IF(n<=$B$2,"Confirmed","Waitlist #"&(n-$B$2))))) for 80 rows, so a cancellation promotes the next person automatically.
5. Tonight: A2:A33 numbers 1-32; B2 =IFERROR(ARRAY_CONSTRAIN(FILTER('Sign-Up'!A5:A84,'Sign-Up'!D5:D84="Confirmed"),32,1),""); a note that names can be typed instead.
6. Rotation: row 3 headers Round, Table, Seat A, Seat B, Seat C, Seat D; A4 =INT((ROW()-4)/8)+1; B4 =MOD(ROW()-4,8)+1; C4 filled to F67: =IF(OR($A4>Settings!$B$5,$B4>Settings!$B$4),"",LET(s,COLUMN()-3,T,Settings!$B$4,p,s*T+MOD($B4-1-s*($A4-1),T)+1,IF(p>Settings!$B$3,"Open seat",INDEX(Tonight!$B$2:$B$33,p)))). Shade alternate rounds; grey out empty rows.
7. Player Lookup: A2:A33 numbers, B name from Tonight, C1:J1 rounds 1-8, C2 =IF(OR($A2>Settings!$B$3,C$1>Settings!$B$5),"",LET(T,Settings!$B$4,s,INT(($A2-1)/T),"Table "&(MOD(MOD($A2-1,T)+s*(C$1-1),T)+1)&" | Seat "&CHAR(65+s))).
8. Night Log: Date, Player (dropdown from Roster names), Games, Wins, Points, Notes.
9. Standings: players from Roster; Nights, Games, Wins, Win %, Points, Avg per game, Rank by points (COUNTIF, SUMIF, RANK); a leaderboard with SORT(FILTER()); top 3 highlighted.
10. Kitty Ledger: Date, Description, Category (Dues, Table fee, Snacks, Prize pool, Supplies, Venue, Other), Who, In, Out, running Balance = opening balance + in - out; category totals with SUMIF.
11. House Rules: editable template covering start time, seating by rotation, phones, guests, cancellations, dues, disputes ("follow the current official rulebook; the host decides"), conduct, and one line honoring mahjong's Chinese origins.
12. Printable Charts: static charts for 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28 and 32 players (numbers, not names), 6 rounds each, computed in the script with the same math (JavaScript mod: ((x%T)+T)%T), each block titled "N players | T tables".
Style: header fill Jade #2F7D6D with white bold text, bands Mist #DCE8E3, top 3 Bamboo Gold #D9A441, waitlist text Cinnabar #B8432F, background Tile Ivory #F7F1E3, text Ink #1F2A36, font Roboto.

ROTATION FACTS (verified; state them and do not change the math): player p sits in seat INT((p-1)/T) (A-D) and starts at table MOD(p-1,T)+1; each round seat A stays, B moves 1 table, C moves 2, D moves 3, wrapping around. Everyone plays every round and every table has 3 or 4 players. Tablemates are all new in rounds 1-2 at 13-16 and 21-24 players, rounds 1-4 at 29-32, rounds 1-5 at 17-20 and rounds 1-7 at 25-28; with 8-12 players some repeats come early and cannot be avoided with 2-3 tables. Seat letters only say where to sit; each table rolls for East as usual.

PART 2. A tab-by-tab table (tab, cell or column, formula or validation) as a manual fallback and QA list.
PART 3. Printable copy, page by page with layout notes: table-number tents 1-8 (US Letter landscape, folded in half), a 24-line sign-up sheet, and a House Rules poster (US Letter; I will also make A4).

RULES: Original wording; no league names, logos or official card content; no real people; no claims about winning or money. Stop after each part and wait for me to type "continue".

SELF-CHECK before each part: formulas use US commas and valid Sheets functions; simulate 30 players and 6 rounds and confirm each name appears once per round and no table has fewer than 3; cancelling a confirmed sign-up promotes Waitlist #1; ledger balance = opening + in - out; standings rank the highest points first. Fix anything that fails, then answer.

assembly: Create a new blank Google Sheet named 'Mahjong Club Organizer Kit' and set File > Settings > Locale to United States (formulas use commas).

Open Extensions > Apps Script, paste the AI's script, save, and run buildClubKit. Approve the authorization screen for your own account (Advanced > Go to project); it only edits this sheet. If it errors, paste the exact error message back to the AI and re-run.

Test before selling: on Tonight type 30 names, set Rounds to 6, and check that Rotation and Player Lookup show each name once per round with no table under 3 players; tick a Cancelled box on Sign-Up and confirm Waitlist #1 becomes Confirmed; add two ledger rows and check the balance.

Clean up: replace the script code with a blank file and save, so buyer copies contain only the spreadsheet; protect formula columns with Data > Protect sheets and ranges > 'Show a warning when editing'; leave the sample data in place with a note to delete it.
Download the Printable Charts tab as PDF (File > Download > PDF, Current sheet, Fit to width, US Letter; repeat with A4).

In Canva build the table-number tents 1-8 (US Letter landscape, folded in half), the 24-line sign-up sheet and the House Rules poster with the Jade Table palette, plus A4 copies at 210 x 297 mm; export PDF Print with no crop marks.

Share the Sheet: General access 'Anyone with the link', Viewer; copy the link and replace everything after the file ID ('/edit...') with '/copy'. Test it in a private window: it should open a 'Make a copy' screen.

Make a 1-page 'Your Club Kit' delivery PDF in Canva with the /copy link as a big button and a 6-step quick start. Record a 15-second screen video (type names, rotation fills) for the Etsy listing video and use screenshots in 2700 x 2025 px (4:3) listing images.
Publish on Etsy with the delivery PDF, the charts PDF and the printables PDF (max 5 files, 20 MB each), and on Gumroad at the same price; add a Gumroad bundle with the instructor kit.

products.superPrompt:
You are a party-stationery designer and a patient mahjong host. Your goal: write and lay out a printable "Holiday Mahjong Night Kit" in three original designs that a host edits, prints at home and uses this December.

BUYER AND JOB: Hosts of holiday mahjong nights (Hanukkah, Christmas, New Year's Eve) and people giving a mahjong set as a gift. Mahjong has become a girls'-night and holiday-hosting favorite; this kit turns a game night into an event and helps first-timers join in without slowing the table.

THREE DESIGNS (identical layouts, different palette and motifs):
A "Festival of Lights" (Hanukkah): Night Blue #1D3557, Candle Gold #E9B949, Silver Mist #D9DEE5, Snow #FAFAF7; motifs: a nine-candle menorah (eight in a row plus one raised helper candle), a dreidel with no letters, small stars.
B "Evergreen" (Christmas): Pine #24523F, Berry #B23A48, Gold #C9A227, Cream #F6F0E3; motifs: pine sprigs, ribbon, a gift box.
C "Midnight" (New Year's Eve): Ink #141414, Champagne #E8D3A2, Silver #BFC5CC, Pearl #F7F5F0; motifs: confetti, streamers, a clock face with no numbers.
Fonts: Playfair Display (headings), Montserrat (body, 10 pt minimum), Great Vibes (names only). White or very light page backgrounds so pages print cheaply.

PIECES (per design; give exact text and layout for each; US Letter landscape sheets, and I will make A4 landscape copies, so keep a 0.25 in safe margin and thin grey cut lines):
1. Invitation, 5x7 in portrait, 2 per sheet: headline, [HOST NAME], [DATE], [TIME], [ADDRESS], [RSVP BY], and "New to mahjong? We'll teach you."
2. Place cards, flat 3.5x4 in folding to 3.5x2 in, 4 per sheet, editable [GUEST NAME].
3. First-timer table tent: a sheet folded in half lengthwise (11x4.25 in faces, one face printed upside down so both sides read): "How a Turn Works" in 5 short steps for American-style play, and a second version for classic Chinese-style tables. Plain, accurate, encouraging.
4. Score pad, half-letter 5.5x8.5 in (A5 for A4), 2 per sheet: table name, date, 4 player columns, 12 game rows, winner, hand value, running totals.
5. Menu card, 5x7 in, 2 per sheet: a cocoa bar and a cocktail-and-mocktail version, each with 4 original drink names and ingredients (at least 2 alcohol-free) and one snack line.
6. Gift sheet: a 3.5x5 in "Lesson Voucher" ("Good for one mahjong lesson with [NAME]") and 6 gift tags at 2x3.5 in, for anyone gifting a set.
7. One instructions page: printing, cutting, folding, editing.

ACCURACY: American turn: draw from the wall (or call the latest discard only to complete an exposure or declare Mah Jongg), add it to your rack, discard one tile face up and name it, play passes to the right; jokers only in groups of three or more, never in a pair or single; match a hand on your current official card to declare Mah Jongg. Classic Chinese-style: most hands are four sets plus a pair. Where rules vary, write "House rules vary." Re-check the menorah description (nine candles).

CONTENT RULES: Original wording, warm and inclusive, about 7th-grade reading level. Mention the card only as "your current official card". Original tile drawings only, shown face-down or with simple dots and bamboo; no Chinese characters drawn by image AI.

DIFFERENTIATION: Score pads alone are common. This kit styles the whole evening in three looks, helps first-timers with table tents, and gives gift-givers a lesson voucher.

CONSTRAINTS: No official card hands, league names or logos, no tile-brand or designer-set names or artwork, no faux-"Asian" novelty fonts or stereotypes, no brand-name drinks or spirits, no song lyrics, no film or TV references, no real people, no health or outcome claims.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Shared text once, then Design A, B and C sheet by sheet as "SHEET n | piece | size and grid | layout | exact text", listing only the lines that change per design (headlines, drink names, motifs). Then a list of illustration assets per design. If you run out of space, stop after a design and wait for me to type "continue".

SELF-CHECK before answering: (1) 3 designs x 7 pieces present; (2) every piece fits its sheet on Letter and A4 landscape with a 0.25 in margin; (3) each menu has at least 2 alcohol-free drinks; (4) turn steps are accurate and say "House rules vary" where needed; (5) no card hands, brand names or stereotyped imagery; (6) all text is original. Fix anything that fails, then answer.
